words: فإن زللتم من بعد ما جاءتكم البينات
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional warning alludes to the community's past associationism and following of desires, presenting their prior lapse as if it had occurred after the proofs came.
rows.anchor: تعريضا بان قومه اشركوا واتبعوا أهواءهم وزلوا فيما مضى من الزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although believers are addressed, the indirect target is the People of the Book, since the lapse belongs to them rather than the believers.
rows.anchor: فان الخطاب للمؤمنين والتعريض لاهل الكتاب لان الزلل لهم لا للمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A conditional can express only the necessary relation between condition and result, without asserting the condition; this works even when it is impossible, necessary, or known to have occurred.
rows.anchor: الشرطية قد لا يراد بها الا مجرد الملازمة التي هي لازمة الشرط والجزاء

words: وما لي لا أعبد الذي فطرني
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker's first-person question indirectly addresses his audience, as shown by the shift to the plural in the following return-to-God phrase; the same indirect address appears in the question about taking other gods.
rows.anchor: المراد ما لكم لا تعبدون بدليل قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Indirect address is courteous: it informs the hearer without confronting him with blame, making acceptance more likely and displaying humility; divine speech uses the audience's idiom to teach the discerning.
rows.anchor: وجه حسنه ظاهر لانه يتضمن اعلام السامع على صورة لا تقتضي مواجهته بالخطاب المنكر

words: لَّا تُسْـَٔلُونَ عَمَّآ أَجْرَمْنَا وَلَا نُسْـَٔلُ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This tactful formulation achieves its aim indirectly; the blunt surface wording would instead say that the audience is not questioned about what we did and we are not questioned about their crimes.
rows.anchor: فحصل المقصود في قالب التلطف وكان حق الحال من حيث الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic can delete the nun of a dual or plural while its grammatical trace remains; the reading al-muqīmī al-ṣalāh illustrates this, as do shortened forms in extended relative clauses.
rows.anchor: حذف نون التثنية والجمع وأثرها باق نحو الضاربا زيدا والضاربو زيدا

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Muʾarrij al-Sadūsī asked al-Akhfash why ya is omitted in wa-l-layli idhā yasri; the answer was that Arabs reduce letters when a word is shifted from its ordinary sense, since night is traveled through rather than traveling.
rows.anchor: ويحكى عن الأخفش أن المؤرج السدوسي سأله عن ذلك فقال لا أجيبك

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummānī explains final ya deletion as preserving the verse ending: endings are treated as if paused, like poetic rhyme.
rows.anchor: وقال الرماني إنما حذفت الياء في الفواصل لأنها على نية الوقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Moses' answer to Pharaoh, the subjects before the repeated Lord descriptions are omitted; Moses magnifies Pharaoh's audacity and points instead to God's distinctive acts, establishing that God has no likeness.
rows.anchor: حذف المبتدأ في ثلاثة مواضع قبل ذكر الرب أي هو رب السموات والله ربكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject is omitted in ṣummun bukmun ʿumyun, with the pronoun hum understood, to spare the tongue from stating it explicitly.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى ﴿ صم بكم عمي ﴾ 6 أي هم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some divine descriptions admit no other implicit subject: ʿālim al-ghayb and faʿʿāl li-mā yurīd are understood of God.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى ﴿ عالم الغيب والشهادة ﴾ 1 ﴿ فعال لما يريد ﴾ 2

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: When an omitted element is so familiar that stating it adds nothing, contextual evidence can speak more clearly than words; al-Zamakhsharī applies this to Hamza's reading, where the preposition before al-arḥām is understood from the preceding phrase.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري وهو نوع من دلالة الحال التي لسانها أنطق من لسان المقال

rows.speaker: الفارسي
rows.claim: Al-Fārisī explains the genitive al-arḥām with an elided repeated preposition, wa-bi-l-arḥām, recoverable from the preceding genitive pronoun.
rows.anchor: قال الفارسي متلخصا من عدم إعادة حرف الجر في المعطوف على الضمير المجرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An omission must be indicated by wording or context; otherwise the expression becomes unintelligible or an inelegant riddle. What remains must guide the reader to what was omitted.
rows.anchor: لا بد أن يكون فيما أبقى دليل على ما ألقى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inflection can signal an omitted governor: on the accusative reading of al-arḥām, an understood command such as wa-iḥfaẓū al-arḥām supplies its case.
rows.anchor: والتقدير احمدوا الحمد واحفظوا الأرحام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meaning and contextual knowledge can require an omitted object; the broad expression yaḥillu wa-yarbiṭu means that someone manages affairs and has full discretion.
rows.anchor: والحالية قد تحصل من النظر إلى المعنى والنظر والعلم فإنه لا يتم إلا بمحذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Syntax can reveal omissions: lā uqsim is understood as la-anā uqsim because a present-tense act is not sworn by, while tafʾat tadhkuru Yūsuf requires a negative lā.
rows.anchor: وقد تدل الصناعة النحوية على التقدير كقولهم في ﴿ لا أقسم بيوم القيامة ﴾ 5 إن التقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A single construction may allow multiple implied comparisons; one reading of afaman zuyyina lahu says it contrasts the beautified sinner with someone whose evil deed was not beautified.
rows.anchor: أحدها كمن لم يزين له سوء عمله والمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conjunction may be omitted when the first of two statements already calls for the second; each then sounds like an independent statement while the mind still links them.
rows.anchor: من حيث إن المتقدم من القولين يستدعي التأخر منهما فلهذا كان الكلام مبنيا على الانفصال

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most grammarians require a separator before coordinating onto an independent nominative pronoun; the examples emphasize the pronoun before adding the conjunct.
rows.anchor: عند الجمهور خلافا لابن مالك في جعله من عطف الجمل

rows.speaker: ابن مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Mālik treats اسكن أنت وزوجك as coordination of clauses, supplying an implicit wa-li-taskun zawjuka rather than coordinating onto the pronoun.
rows.anchor: خلافا لابن مالك في جعله من عطف الجمل بتقدير ولتسكن زوجك

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: On the reading with an open wāw, al-Zamakhsharī analyzes aw ābāʾunā in the resurrection question as a conjunct on the pronoun, with the hamza as separator.
rows.anchor: وجعل الزمخشري منه ﴿ أئنا لمبعوثون أو آباؤنا ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposed analysis of aw ābāʾunā is challenged because an interrogative hamza does not govern an isolated noun.
rows.anchor: ورد بان الاستفهام لايدخل على المفردات

rows.speaker: الفارسي
rows.claim: Al-Fārisī gives mā ashraknā wa-lā ābāʾunā as another coordination example; Ibn al-Dahhān instead parses wa-lā ābāʾunā as a subject with an implicit predicate, ashrakū.
rows.anchor: وجعل الفارسي منه ﴿ ما أشركنا ولا آباؤنا ﴾ 8 واعرب ابن الدهان

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans allow coordination onto a pronoun without an intervening separator, citing wa-alladhīna hādū wa-l-ṣābiʾūn.
rows.anchor: وأجاز الكوفيون العطف من غير فاصل كقوله تعالى ﴿ والذين هادوا والصابئون ﴾

rows.speaker: الفارسي
rows.claim: Al-Fārisī parses wa-huwa as a fresh subject rather than a conjunct on the pronoun in fastawā; he also says a genitive pronoun cannot be coordinated onto without repeating its preposition.
rows.anchor: فقال الفارسي ﴿ وهو ﴾ مبتدأ وليس معطوفا على ضمير ﴿ فاستوى ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In wa-min Nūḥ, repeating the preposition is required if the phrase joins mink, but is optional if it joins al-nabiyyīn.
rows.anchor: فان جعلنا ﴿ ومن نوح ﴾ معطوفا على ﴿ منك ﴾ فالاعادة لازمة وان جعل معطوفا على ﴿ النبيين ﴾ فجائزة

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufans say a preposition need not be repeated before a conjunct on a genitive pronoun, citing Hamza's genitive reading al-arḥām; an alternative parses it as an oath.
rows.anchor: وقال الكوفيون لاتلزم الاعادة محتجين بآيات الاولى قراءة حمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān is the revelation given to Muhammad for exposition and inimitability, whereas readings are variations in its written letters or their performance, such as lightening and doubling.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن القرآن والقراءات حقيقتان متغايرتان فالقرآن هو الوحى المنزل على محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Dānī's al-Taysīr is recommended for the seven readings; al-Shāṭibī versified it, Ibn al-Bādhish wrote al-Iqnāʿ, and al-Shahrazūrī's al-Miṣbāḥ covers the ten readings.
rows.anchor: وأحسن الموضوع للقراءات السبع كتاب التيسير لأبى عمرو الدانى وقد نظمه أبو محمد القاسم الشاطبى

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority regard the seven readings as mass-transmitted, while another view calls them merely well-known.
rows.anchor: القراءات السبع متواترة عند الجمهور وقيل بل مشهورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objections of al-Mubarrad to Hamza's al-arḥām and miṣrikhī, and of Ibn ʿAṣfūr to Ibn ʿĀmir's reading, do not count against the canonical readings.
rows.anchor: ولا عبرة بإنكار المبرد قراءة حمزة ﴿ والأرحام ﴾ و / مصرخي /

rows.speaker: أبو شامة
rows.claim: Abū Shāma noted that the documented chains for the seven readings pass from one transmitter to another and do not uniformly meet the conditions of mass transmission at every level.
rows.anchor: وقد أشار الشيخ شهاب الدين أبو شامة في كتابه المرشد الوجيز إلى شيء من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven readings are mass-transmitted from their seven imams, though whether that transmission is mass-transmitted all the way back to the Prophet requires qualification.
rows.anchor: والتحقيق أنها متواترة عن الأئمة السبعة أما تواترها عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ففيه نظر

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو بن الحاجب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Ḥājib excludes performance features such as lengthening, imāla, and easing hamza from the claim that the seven readings are mass-transmitted.
rows.anchor: استثنى الشيخ أبو عمرو بن الحاجب قولنا إن القراءات السبع متواترة ما ليس من قبيل الأداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exclusion is weak: lengthening and imāla are certainly mass-transmitted as shared categories, although readers differ over their degree.
rows.anchor: وهذا ضعيف والحق أن المد والإمالة لا شك في تواتر المشترك بينهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers differ in measured length: Hamza and Warsh use six units, with reports of five or four; ʿĀṣim uses three, al-Kisāʾī two and a half, Qālūn two, and al-Sūsī one and a half.
rows.anchor: فحمزة وورش بمقدار ست لغات وقيل خمس وقيل أربع وعن عاصم ثلاث

rows.speaker: ابن الحاجب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Ḥājib explains that an interrogative hamza is followed by a long vowel before an open wasl hamza to avoid confusing a question with a statement, as in āl-ḥasanu ʿindak.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الحاجب في تصريفه واغتفر التقاء الساكنين في نحو آلحسن عندك وآيمن الله يمينك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Arabs soften the wasl hamza between two pronunciations; readers transmit both forms, though the lengthened form is standard, and the Uthmanic spelling of a second hamza as wāw signals the softened form.
rows.anchor: وبعض العرب يجعل همزة الوصل فيما ذكرنا بين بين ويقول آلحسن عندك وآيمن الله يمينك

rows.speaker: الشاطبي
rows.claim: For two hamzas in separate words with matching vowels, Abū ʿAmr drops the first according to al-Shāṭibī; another view says the second is dropped, as in jāʾa ajaluhum.
rows.anchor: وقد قرأ به أبو عمرو في الهمزتين من كلمتين إذا اتفقتا في الحركة فأسقط الأولى منهما على رأي الشاطبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the open-hamza case, Nāfiʿ through Qālūn and Ibn Kathīr through al-Bazzī also transmit dropping a hamza; Qunbul transmits its deletion within the single word shirkāʾī.
rows.anchor: ووافقه على ذلك في المفتوحتين نافع من طريق قالون وابن كثير من طريق البزي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurʾānic readings are fixed by transmission, not selected through grammarians' taste or eloquent reasoning; this rejects al-Zamakhsharī's criticism of Hamza's genitive al-arḥām and other disputed readings.
rows.anchor: أن القراءات توقيفية وليست اختيارية خلافا لجماعة منهم الزمخشري حيث ظنوا أنها اختيارية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people under discussion were already believers, as the occasion of revelation shows; the wording's possessive attribution treats them this way to intensify encouragement.
rows.anchor: قلت كانوا مؤمنين قبله بدليل سبب نزولها وعوملوا هذه المعاملة من الإضافة مبالغة في الترغيب

words: ومن يعص الله ورسوله ويتعد حدوده
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat of eternal fire is a deterrent, not a literal universal denial of forgiveness: taking the conditional generic man to cover every sin would make all sinners eternally damned, contradicting forgiveness.
rows.anchor: يدل على قصد مجرد الترهيب بطلان النصوصية من ظاهرها على عدم المغفرة لأهل المعاصى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Expressions can differ in eloquence through the force and dignity of individual meanings and through smoothness of wording.
rows.anchor: أحدها المعانى الإفرادية بأن يكون بعضها أقوى دلالة وأفخم مسمى وأسلس لفظا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inflection can make an expression more eloquent: wa-shtaʿala al-raʾsu shayban uses a specification construction that is stronger than shaybatan or shayba al-raʾs.
rows.anchor: الثانى المعانى الإعرابية بأن يكون مسماها أبلغ معنى كالتمييز مع البدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Syntactic arrangement can improve meaning: in lā tattakhidhū ilāhayni ithnayn, ithnayn is the object and ilāhayni a fronted adjective, with the broader term ithnayn emphasized.
rows.anchor: الثالث مواقع التركيب كعوله تعالى ﴿ وقال الله لا تتخذوا إلهين اثنين ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān's highest form of inimitability lies in a composition whose arrangement cannot be made more fitting or balanced for conveying its meaning.
rows.anchor: فصل فى اشتمال القرآن على أعلى أنواع الإعجاز وهو أن يقع التركيب بحيث لا يمتنع

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر ابن الطيب
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr ibn al-Ṭayyib denies degrees of eloquence in the Qurʾān: every word is at the highest level, though people differ in how well they perceive it.
rows.anchor: واختار القاضى أبو بكر ابن الطيب فى كتاب ( الإعجاز ) المنع وأن كل كلمة موصوفة بالذروة العليا

rows.speaker: أبو بصر بن القشيري
rows.claim: Abū Baṣr ibn al-Qushayrī accepts that Qurʾānic eloquence has degrees and rebukes grammarians for weakening Hamza's genitive al-arḥām.
rows.anchor: واختار أبو بصر بن القشيرى فى تفسيره التفاوت

rows.speaker: أبو بصر بن القشيري
rows.claim: He argues that rejecting a reading established from the Prophet is perilous; Arabic is learned from the Prophet, whose eloquence is beyond doubt, rather than from language authorities who criticize it.
rows.anchor: واختار أبو بصر بن القشيرى فى تفسيره التفاوت فقال وقد رد على الزجاج وغيره تضعيفهم قراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grammarians may only have meant that Hamza's reading is sound and eloquent though another reading is more eloquent; not every Qurʾānic expression must be at the highest degree.
rows.anchor: ولعلهم أرادوا أنه صحيح فصيح وإن كان غيره أفصح منه فإنا لا ندعى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Singling out two figures after mentioning the angels can honor them despite their belonging to that same genus; the wording may also treat the pair numerically as three, while the added specification itself signals distinction.
rows.anchor: وذكرهما بعد الملائكة مع كونهما من الجنس دليل على قصد التنويه بشرفهما

words: وَخَلَقَكُم مِّن نَّفْسٍۢ وَٰحِدَةٍۢ وَخَلَقَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars differ whether a specific member stated after a general term was already included; the added mention can be emphatic, and al-Rūyānī reports a related two-view dispute in a bequest case.
rows.anchor: وأيضا فالخلاف السابق في أن ذكر بعض افراد العام بعد العام هل يدل على انه لم يدخل في العام

words: وَخَلَقَكُم مِّن نَّفْسٍۢ وَٰحِدَةٍۢ وَخَلَقَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا
rows.speaker: الروياني
rows.claim: Al-Rūyānī reports two views on whether a poor Zayd receives both a named dinar and a share of a bequest to the poor; the stronger view gives him only the dinar because the specification limits the executor's discretion.
rows.anchor: وحكاه الروياني في البحر من كتاب الوصية وخرد عليه ما إذا أوصى رجل لزيد بدينار

words: وَخَلَقَكُم مِّن نَّفْسٍۢ وَٰحِدَةٍۢ وَخَلَقَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا
rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī and Ibn Jinnī say a specifically named member is not included in the general expression; on that view, this verse is not an example of the rule.
rows.anchor: والقول بعدم دخوله تحت اللفظ هو قول أبي علي الفارسي وتلميذه ابن جني

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī sometimes allows a later conjunct to attach either to the first conjunct or to the nearer preceding phrase.
rows.anchor: فإذا اجتمع في الكلام معطوفان هل يجعل الآخر معطوفا على الأول أو على ما يليه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī attaches mukhrij al-mayyit to fāliq rather than yukh’rij, avoiding coordination of a noun with a verb; Ibn Mālik disagrees and offers another analysis.
rows.anchor: فذكر في قوله تعالى ﴿ إن الله فالق الحب والنوى يخرج الحي من الميت ومخرج الميت من الحي ﴾ أن مخرجا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads al-malāʾikah in the phrase about God's coming as coordinated with Allah, linking it to the eternal decree.
rows.anchor: وذكر ايضا في قوله تعالى ﴿ إلا أن يأتيهم الله في ظلل من الغمام والملائكة وقضي الأمر ﴾

words: وَخَلَقَكُم مِّن نَّفْسٍۢ وَٰحِدَةٍۢ وَخَلَقَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا وَبَثَّ مِنْهُمَا رِجَالًۭا كَثِيرًۭا وَنِسَآءًۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If yā ayyuhā al-nās is universal, wa-khalaqa minhā zawjahā coordinates with an omitted verb, meaning He originated and brought her into being; if addressed to Meccans, khalaqa coordinates with khalaqakum, avoiding repetition.
rows.anchor: حاصله أن قوله ﴿ يا أيها الناس ﴾ إذا اريد به العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text commonly gives precedence to men as a mark of their distinction, as in its mention of many men and women.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ رجالا كثيرا ونساء ﴾ 6

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Precedence can mark distinctions in prophethood, freedom, reason, faith, knowledge, life, and the nobility of what is known; the cited examples place the more honored item first.
rows.anchor: ومنها شرف الإيمان كقوله تعالى ﴿ وإن كان طائفة منكم آمنوا بالذي أرسلت به وطائفة لم يؤمنوا ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When daughters are named first in the gift of children, the order compensates them as a vulnerable group; the definiteness used for sons compensates them for losing precedence.
rows.anchor: فلجبرهن إذ هن موضع الانكسار ولهذا جبر الذكور بالتعريف للإشارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible reason for naming daughters first is to show that all creation follows God's will rather than human preference.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن تقديم الإناث لأن المقصود بيان أن الخلق كله بمشيئة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other orderings follow causal or temporal priority: livestock precede people as the cause, and death precedes life because it existed earlier.
rows.anchor: فمن باب تقديم السبب وقد سبق

rows.speaker: القرطبي
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī reports an unusual dispute over whether a free person is more noble than an enslaved person and directs readers to the discussion in his Sūrat al-Nisāʾ commentary.
rows.anchor: ومن الغريب حكاية بعضهم قولين في أن الحر أشرف من العبد أم لا حكاه القرطبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unseen is nobler than what is witnessed, explaining the order in ʿālim al-ghayb wa-l-shahādah.
rows.anchor: ومنها شرف المعلوم نحو ﴿ عالم الغيب والشهادة ﴾ 9 فإن علم الغيبيات أشرف من المشاهدات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takbīr from the opening of Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā through the Qurʾān's end is the Meccan reading, transmitted by Ibn Kathīr from Mujāhid, Ibn ʿAbbās, Ubayy, and the Prophet; Ibn Khuzayma and al-Bayhaqī report it, and al-Bayhaqī strengthens it.
rows.anchor: وهي قراءة أهل مكة أخذها ابن كثير عن مجاهد عن ابن عباس وابن عباس عن أبي وأبي عن النبي

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم الرازي
rows.claim: A mawqūf report from Ubayy has a known chain but is called rare; Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī rejected the report, consistently with his strict approach.
rows.anchor: ورواه من طريق موقوفا على أبي بسند معروف وهو حديث غريب وقد أنكره أبو حاتم الرازي

rows.speaker: الحليمي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥalīmī supports the practice by analogy: a completed Qurʾānic reading resembles completing a month, for which people are told to magnify God.
rows.anchor: واستأنس له الحليمي بأن القراءة تنقسم إلى أبعاض متفرقة فكأنه كصيام الشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others explain the takbīr as marking the felt end of revelation; after each sūra the reader pauses, says Allāhu akbar, pauses again, then begins the next sūra.
rows.anchor: وذكر غيره أن التكبير كان لاستشعار انقطاع الوحى قال وصفته فى آخر هذه السور

rows.speaker: سليم الرازي
rows.claim: Sulaym al-Rāzī says Ibn Kathīr's reader begins the takbīr at al-Ḍuḥā, separates it from each sūra with a pause, and continues between sūras until the end.
rows.anchor: وقال سليم الرازي في تفسيره يكبر القارىء بقراءة ابن كثير إذا بلغ والضحى

rows.speaker: سليم الرازي
rows.claim: Sulaym links the practice to the revelation's delay: people said Muhammad had been deserted and disliked, then al-Ḍuḥā was revealed and the Prophet said Allāhu akbar.
rows.anchor: وكأن المعنى فى ذلك ما روى أن الوحى كان تأخر عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أياما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other readers do not use takbīr; they argue it risks adding material to the Qurʾān if people mistake the formula for Qurʾānic text and record it.
rows.anchor: ولا يكبر فى قراءة الباقين ومن حجتهم أن فى ذلك ذريعة إلى الزيادة فى القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Across the Qurʾān, saʿīr means fire or its fuel, except in fī ḍalālin wa-suʿur, where it means obstinacy or madness.
rows.anchor: وكل شىء فى القرآن من ذكر السعير فهو النار والوقود إلا قوله عز وجل ﴿ إن المجرمين في ضلال وسعر ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shayṭān generally means Iblīs, his followers, and descendants; in shayāṭīnihim it means their soothsayers, including Kaʿb al-Ashraf, Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab, and his brother Abū Yāsir.
rows.anchor: وكل شىء فى القرآن من ذكر شيطان فإنه إبليس وجنوده وذريته إلا قوله تعالى فى سورة البقرة ﴿ وإذا خلوا إلى شياطينهم ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shahīd usually means a witness to people's affairs, apart from references to those killed in battle; in wadʿū shuhadāʾakum it means your partners.
rows.anchor: وكل شهيد في القرآن غير القتلى في الغزو فهم الذين يشهدون على أمور الناس

words: وَمَا جَعَلْنَآ أَصْحَٰبَ ٱلنَّارِ إِلَّا مَلَٰٓئِكَةًۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aṣḥāb al-nār normally means the people of the Fire; in this verse it refers to the Fire's keepers.
rows.anchor: وكل ما فى القرآن من أصحاب النار فهم اهل النار إلا قوله ﴿ وما جعلنا أصحاب النار إلا ملائكة ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣalāh generally denotes worship or mercy; in the phrase ṣalawāt wa-masājid it means houses of worship.
rows.anchor: وكل صلاة فى القرآن فهى عبادة ورحمة إلا قوله تعالى ﴿ وصلوات ومساجد ﴾ فإنه يريد بيوت عبادتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deafness usually describes refusal to hear faith, except in the Banū Isrāʾīl passage where ṣumman means literally unable to hear anything.
rows.anchor: وكل صمم في القرآن فهو عن الاستماع للإيمان غير واحد في بني اسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAdhāb ordinarily means punishment or chastisement; here it specifically means beating.
rows.anchor: وكل عذاب فى القرآن فهو التعذيب إلا قوله عز وجل ﴿ وليشهد عذابهما ﴾ فإنه يريد الضرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qānitūn usually means obedient, but in the cited verses in al-Baqara and al-Rūm it means acknowledging God's lordship and servitude.
rows.anchor: والقانتون المطيعون لكن قوله عز وجل فى البقرة ﴿ كل له قانتون ﴾ معناه مقرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kanz normally means wealth; the treasure beneath the wall in the Cave story is written pages and knowledge.
rows.anchor: وكل كنز فى القرآن فهو المال إلا الذى فى سورة الكهف ﴿ وكان تحته كنز لهما ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miṣbāḥ usually means a star; in the Light verse it means the lamp itself.
rows.anchor: وكل مصباح فى القرآن فهو الكوكب إلا الذى فى سورة النور ﴿ المصباح في زجاجة ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nikāḥ generally means marriage, but in this verse it denotes puberty.
rows.anchor: النكاح فى القرآن التزوج إلا قوله جل ثناؤه ﴿ حتى إذا بلغوا النكاح ﴾ فإنه يعنى الحلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabaʾ and anbāʾ normally mean reports; in this verse al-anbāʾ means proofs or arguments.
rows.anchor: النبأ والأنباء فى القرآن الأخبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Warada usually means to enter; when Moses came to the water of Midian, it means he approached it without entering.
rows.anchor: الورود فى القرآن الدخول إلا فى القصص

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: The permission sense of min allows either recipient in a pair, as in jālis al-Ḥasan wa-Ibn Sīrīn; Mālik applies this reading to the charitable recipient classes in the alms verse.
rows.anchor: الرابع للإباحة نحو جالس الحسن وابن سيرين لأنك أمرت بمجالستهما معا

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: A reported wāw al-thamāniyya marks completion at eight, since seven is the Arabs' complete number; al-Baghawī transmits this theory through ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jābir from Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbdūs.
rows.anchor: حكاه البغوي عن عبدالله بن جابر عن أبي بكر بن عبدوس ويدل عليه قوله تعالى ﴿ سبع ليال وثمانية أيام ﴾

rows.speaker: ابن خالويه
rows.claim: Ibn Khālawayh and others cite thāminuhum kalbuhum after two earlier counts without wāw, and the differing door descriptions of Paradise and Hell, as evidence for the eight-marker theory.
rows.anchor: ونقل عن ابن خالويه وغيره ومثلوه بقوله تعالى ﴿ وثامنهم كلبهم ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-l-nāhūna ʿan al-munkar follows several traits without wāw; one explanation is that forbidding wrong occurs at the same time as enjoining right, though they remain distinct acts.
rows.anchor: وقيل دخلت فيه أعلاما بأن الآمر بالمعروف ناه عن المنكر في حال أمره بالمعروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thayyibāt wa-abkār is not an example of the eight-marker wāw: omitting the conjunction would make the contradictory descriptions impossible.
rows.anchor: من هذا القبيل خلافا لبعضهم لأن الواو لو اسقطت منه لاستحال المعنى

rows.speaker: المحققون
rows.claim: The more exacting scholars do not recognize a special eight-marker; they parse the examples as ordinary coordination or circumstantial wāw, with Paradise's gates already open before its people arrive and Hell's still closed.
rows.anchor: ولم يثبت المحققون واو الثمانية وأولوا ما سبق على العطف أو واو الحال

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another explanation says the wāw in Paradise's description marks God's mercy as exceeding His anger and punishment.
rows.anchor: وقيل زيدت في صفة الجنة علامة لزيادة رحمة الله على غضبه وعقوبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that wāw occurs among adjectives only when the attributes repeat is incorrect.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أنها لا تأتي في الصفات إلا إذا تكررت النعوت وليس كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An incomplete pause after ʿiwajā clarifies that qayyiman is separate from ʿiwajā and is a circumstantial phrase whose syntactic position is advanced.
rows.anchor: منها أن يكون لضرب من البيان كقوله تعالى ﴿ ولم يجعل له عوجا قيما ﴾ إذ به تبين أن قيما منفصل عن عوجا

words: وَعَمَّٰتُكُمْ وَخَٰلَٰتُكُمْ وَبَنَاتُ ٱلْأَخِ وَبَنَاتُ ٱلْأُخْتِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pause between the listed aunts and nieces clarifies the boundary between prohibitions by blood relation and those by marriage.
rows.anchor: وكما في قوله تعالى ﴿ وعماتكم وخالاتكم وبنات الأخ وبنات الأخت ﴾ ليفصل به بين التحريم النسبي والسببي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pausing after hādhā in the revived people's exclamation shows that hādhā is not part of their quoted speech.
rows.anchor: قلت ومنه قوله تعالى ﴿ يا ويلنا من بعثنا من مرقدنا هذا ﴾ ليبين أن هذا ليس من مقولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A permissible incomplete pause may have the same surface form as continuous recitation, as at the end of wa-tawallā in the description of the Fire.
rows.anchor: ومنها أن تكون صورته فى اللفظ صورة الوصل بعينها نحو قوله تعالى ﴿ كلا إنها لظى نزاعة للشوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some wording is constructed to require a pause, as in the speaker's wish that he had not received his record; the author contrasts a complete-stop example ending in nār ḥāmiyah.
rows.anchor: ومنها أن يكون الكلام مبنيا على الوقف فلا يجوز فيه إلا الوقف صيغة كقوله ﴿ يا ليتني لم أوت كتابيه
